transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Neeta Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Wavefront), Omar Haddad (Wavefront CTO), Samir Khan (Wavefront), June Park (Wavefront Security)

Summary: Quickstart SDK walkthrough for Python and TypeScript, auth patterns (API key vs OIDC service account), environment bootstrapping, and a short demo of Console + Optimize suggestions. Discussed pilot scope and security requirements.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through a hands-on quickstart today, so we'll cover the python and ts sdks, how to wire up auth in a cloud env, and then show the Console Optimize suggestions. feel free to interrupt.
[00:23] Priya Desai: thanks Maya, quick ask — i'm primarily integrating from a backend service running in k8s, node + python microservices. want to understand recommended auth flow and how secrets sit in k8s.
[00:35] Lucas Rivera: cool, that's common. we'll show both approaches: short-lived OIDC tokens for service accounts (recommended for private deployment / vpc) and api key env var for hosted/quickstart. in k8s we usually recommend sealed secrets or your cloud secret manager, and we provide an example using gcp workload identity in the repo.
[01:02] Priya: perfect, also curious about env var scoping — we run multiple stages (dev/stage/prod) and want least privilege.
[01:10] Maya: yes, quickstart includes separate config files and an example dockerfile. we also show how to pin models and set request timeouts.
[01:24] Samir Khan: is there a node ts example for streaming responses? low-latency chat path is our priority so want to see that.
[01:32] Neeta Patel: yes, the ts sdk supports streaming with an async iterator pattern, we'll demo it after the auth bits. note, streaming is slightly different when you route to a dedicated pool vs hosted — latency SLOs change.
[02:10] Omar Haddad: security side, June will ask about keys, kms, and audit logs — what do you provide out of the box?
[02:21] June Park: hi, thanks — two things: 1) do you support customer KMS for model input encryption at rest, and 2) audit logs for every inference request at token level?
[02:33] Lucas: short answer: yes to audit logs — we can emit request/response metadata to your logging sink and we support detailed tracing in Console. for KMS we support customer-managed keys for private deployments and dedicated instances via integration with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault. for hosted accounts we offer envelope encryption and rotation, and an enterprise option for customer KMS.
[03:05] Maya: i can share the security whitepaper and the kms integration guide after the call.
[03:11] Priya: great. can you also show how Optimize suggests batching and quantization settings? we saw a note in the docs but want details.
[03:20] Neeta: absolutely — Optimize inspects your traffic shape and suggests batch sizes, kv cache settings, and quantization profiles. we'll show a sample recommendation where Optimize boosted throughput by ~2.6x for a retrieval-augmented workflow we ran.
[03:44] Samir: cool. for the quickstart repo, will it have a sample prompt set and evals to test quality regressions?
[03:51] Lucas: yes, the repo contains a tiny eval harness and a sample prompt set under /evals with instructions for local runs.

-- Quickstart and Auth Walkthrough --
[04:12] Maya: switching to screen share — i'm opening the quickstart README. the repo url is pinned in the calendar but i'll paste in chat afterwards.
[04:31] Maya: first file is the .env.example — you'll see REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_URL for hosted. for private/dedicated we also show REDWOOD_OIDC_TOKEN_PATH for a workload identity file.
[05:02] Priya: curious, what's the shape of the token file? is it just a jwt?
[05:09] Lucas: yeah it's a standard OIDC jwt, short-lived. the SDK will pick it up if you set REDWOOD_AUTH_TYPE=oidc and REDWOOD_OIDC_TOKEN_PATH=/var/run/secrets/redwood/token. fallback is api_key when present.
[05:35] Samir: i usually use env vars in k8s, but rotating keys is a pain. how do you recommend rotations?
[05:42] Neeta: rotate in your secret manager and the sdks pick up new tokens; for api keys we recommend programmatically fetching rotated keys into a k8s secret via a small operator or your cloud secret sync. we include a sample helm hook in the repo.
[06:05] Maya: note — for dedicated pools you can also issue scoped service accounts with rate limits per account, so rotations and least privilege are simpler.

[06:38] Lucas: moving to code: python quickstart, file quickstart/python/app.py — main call uses from redwood import RedwoodClient, model = client.model('redwood/fast-chat') — we then show streaming and function calling.
[07:05] Priya: can you show the call signature? we'd like to understand token usage per call and how to control stop sequences and max tokens.
[07:15] Lucas: sure — client.generate(model='...', input='prompt', max_tokens=512, stop=['

']) — tokens are charged by the model, and the client exposes request metadata for latency and token counts per response in the return object.
[07:41] Samir: does the SDK expose native retry/backoff helpers? sometimes our network flaps.
[07:48] Lucas: yes, built-in retry with exponential backoff and jitter. you can override policies per-call or set a global transport retry policy.

[08:20] Maya: switching to TS example — quickstart/ts/app.ts — we show usage with import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) ...
[08:44] Samir: and the streaming example looks different in ts?
[08:50] Neeta: it's an async iterator: for await (const chunk of client.stream(...)) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta) } — same semantics as python but different surface.

[09:20] Priya: you'd mentioned pinning models for consistent behavior — can we pin a model version in both sdks and on the Console?
[09:29] Lucas: yes, pin via model: 'redwood/fast-chat@v1.2.0' or via route config in Console. Console rollout supports canary and A/B and shows per-variant metrics.
[09:47] Omar: what's the expected integration time for our team? we have two sde's and one platform eng who's doing infra.
[09:56] Maya: most teams get the quickstart wired in a day or two and a production pilot in 2–4 weeks depending on evals and security signoffs.

-- Demo: Console + Optimize --
[10:28] Neeta: now i'm in Console, i'll pull up a demo account. here's the traffic heatmap, token cost by route, and Optimize suggestions panel.
[10:45] Neeta: for this route, Optimize suggested: enable prefix caching for the first 128 tokens, increase batch size to 8 for p95 sequence length of 120, and use int8 quantization for non-critical models. gives estimated cost savings ~34%.
[11:07] Priya: how do we validate quality after quantization? we can't have regressions in our summarization quality.
[11:16] Neeta: we recommend running the eval harness in the quickstart against the quantized variant. Console also supports regression alerts — it can compare outputs on a golden prompt set and trigger an alert if rouge/bertscore drops.
[11:41] Omar: can Optimize be run offline against a historical traffic dump? we may want to simulate before applying to prod.
[11:52] Neeta: yes, you can upload traces or run a local simulation in the repo; we'll share a script that replays requests and measures latency/cost across profiles.

[12:25] Samir: about rate limiting — we have some bursty patterns from nightly batch jobs. how do you handle throttling?
[12:34] Lucas: Console allows per-route quotas and token-based rate limits. we also support burst capacity on Dedicated, and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if your primary model is at capacity.
[12:55] Priya: that fallback — is it automatic or do we configure it?
[13:00] Maya: both: we have automatic fallback policies you can enable, and you can also set explicit route-level fallbacks with custom transform rules.

[13:30] June Park: audit logs — do you provide a S3-style export or streaming to our SIEM?
[13:38] Lucas: both options. you can push logs to a customer-owned bucket or stream to Splunk/Datadog via our connector. logs can be redacted to avoid PII.

[14:02] Priya: demo time — can you show a sample integration where node does a streaming chat and python does an embedding call for search?
[14:10] Neeta: sure — opening sample app: node route /chat uses client.stream with an onChunk handler that updates UI; python worker uses client.embed(['docs...']) and writes vectors to Pinecone (example). code snippet incoming.
[14:36] Maya: note that the example uses async retries around embed calls and a fixed backoff; it's intentionally simple so teams can extend.

[15:00] (Audio glitch, brief silence)
[15:22] Omar: sorry, had a quick call, we're back.
[15:29] Priya: no problem. continuing.

[15:42] Samir: about local dev — does the SDK support a mocked offline mode? we'd like tests to run without hitting the network.
[15:50] Lucas: yes, quickstart includes a mock server that implements the basic endpoints. you can run npm run mock-server or python -m redwood.mock. it returns canned streaming deltas for UI tests.

[16:20] Priya: any tips for measuring token footprint during development? we'd like to keep costs predictable.
[16:29] Neeta: use the RequestTelemetry wrapper we provide — it annotates each call with token usage and aggregates to Prometheus metrics. Console can ingest that to show per-route cost.

[17:05] Maya: slightly shifting — pilot considerations. what's a good success criteria?
[17:12] Priya: for us, latency p95 < 250ms for chat, average cost per full response < $0.12, and no regression in summary F1 vs baseline.
[17:24] Omar: we also need proof of data residency and an audit log retention policy for 12 months.
[17:30] Maya: understood — we'll include deployment diagrams and retention settings.

[17:48] Lucas: quick note on telemetry — when you run the smoke test we'll collect p50/p95 latencies, token counts, and error rates. we'll export a spreadsheet with per-route breakdowns.

[18:16] Neeta: showing the console route config editor — you can toggle "enforce model pin", "allow fallback", and set "batching policy" (auto/manual). setting batch policy to auto uses Optimize suggestions during peak hours only.
[18:44] Samir: if auto batching increases latency for 99th percentile, can we disable it per-route?
[18:50] Neeta: yes, route-level overrides exist. you can also set a max latency SLO to prevent batching from exceeding it.

[19:15] Priya: if we go with dedicated for pilot, what does onboarding look like? infra we need to provision?
[19:23] Maya: for Dedicated we provision GPU pools, we provide terraform modules for the VPC peering, and we guide you on KMS, IAM roles, and a bootstrap script to register nodes. typical lead time is 2–3 weeks depending on cloud approvals.
[19:40] Omar: and is there a staging cluster option? we want dev/stage/prod separation.
[19:46] Maya: yes we can provision multiple pools or you can use namespaces + route separation. audit logs and Console support multi-environment views.

[20:12] Lucas: small demo — i'll send a streaming chat from node to show chunked deltas. (typing sounds)
[20:25] Lucas: (node) for await (const c of client.stream({model:'redwood/fast-chat', input: 'Summarize the attached meeting notes'})) { console.log(c.delta) }
[20:41] (console output) "- The quickstart includes env examples..."
[20:48] Priya: that looks straightforward.

[21:10] Samir: on embeddings, any recommendation for vector store? we use pinecone but open to alternatives.
[21:17] Neeta: Pinecone is good; we show connectors for Pinecone, Weaviate, and an S3+FAISS example if you prefer self-hosted.

[21:45] Priya: are there SDK gauges around token batching vs streaming? how do they interplay?
[21:53] Lucas: streaming streams tokens as they come back; batching is at request-level before being sent to the model. they are orthogonal but Optimize coordinates them — if you enable streaming, Optimize will avoid batching policies that increase latency too much.

[22:34] (15 second side discussion about calendar invites)

[23:00] Maya: let's talk pilot scope: Priya, you mentioned a retrieval-augmented summarization flow — would you be ok starting with 100k monthly tokens and a small test set?
[23:10] Priya: yes, that's fine for initial accuracy checks.
[23:18] Omar: also want to run a cost-sensitivity test: what happens if we quantize and move to a cheaper model? need to see quality delta.
[23:26] Neeta: we'll include that in the smoke test plan — run baseline, int8, and a fallback cheaper variant and capture eval metrics.

[24:00] Maya: i realize we're already 24 minutes in, want to speed through the repo mapping and then set next steps.
[24:08] Lucas: repo layout: /quickstart/python, /quickstart/ts, /evals, /infra/helm, /mock, /scripts/replay.py. lookup table in README.
[24:32] Priya: can we see the sample infra/helm to validate service account bindings?
[24:37] Lucas: yes — helm chart includes a workloadIdentity config and secret sync hook.

[25:05] Priya: question on SSO — can SAML be used for Console access and RBAC?
[25:11] Maya: yes, Console supports SAML, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access control. we'll include a sample SAML metadata file in the support packet.

[25:45] June Park: data residency — for hosted accounts can you guarantee EU-only?
[25:53] Maya: hosted accounts can be region-restricted; for firm guarantees enterprise Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended for strict residency.

[26:20] Samir: will the quickstart include a .github actions workflow to run evals on PRs?
[26:27] Lucas: yes there's an example workflow that runs small evals and fails if regression thresholds are exceeded.

[27:00] (brief cross-talk about a link paste)

[27:30] Maya: i'll recap next steps at the end but first, final technical Qs?
[27:38] Priya: one more— are there SDK telemetry knobs to disable sending full request text to Console? we need to avoid sending PII.
[27:46] Neeta: yes, you can redact at the SDK level or set Console ingest to redact. the quickstart includes a redaction middleware sample.

[28:10] Omar: for the perf smoke test — we prefer a scoped run against a dedicated single instance to get conservative numbers — can Lucas run that?
[28:18] Lucas: yes i'm planning a 2-hour run next Tue; will attach results and the spreadsheet.

[28:44] Priya: can you share a sample of the rollouts screen where we configure canary at 10%?
[28:52] Neeta: pulling it up now — here's create rollout, set canary 10%, monitor for 30m, auto-rollback on error rate > 1%.

[29:12] Samir: small nit — SDK versions and semver? do you guarantee no breaking changes in minor releases?
[29:19] Maya: we follow semver, breaking changes only on major. we also publish migration notes in the repo.

[29:45] (short pause)

[30:00] Maya: OK recapping: Maya will share quickstart repo + security pack, Lucas will run perf smoke test and share results, Neeta will add RBAC snippets and sample rollout docs. Priya/Omar will confirm pilot prompt list.

[30:20] Priya: timeline — can we aim to start pilot week of 10/13?
[30:25] Omar: yes that aligns with our roadmap.

[30:40] Maya: great — i'll put a follow-up invite for 10/15 for pilot kickoff.

[31:00] (conversation drifts into small implementation clarifications, snippets read aloud)

[35:12] Priya: one more question — how do we instrument canary metrics? i want trace-level sampling.
[35:20] Lucas: Console supports trace sampling and you can configure per-route trace percent; we'll also provide a tracing hook you can plug into OpenTelemetry.

[36:05] Neeta: showing an example of Optimize suggestion history — you can compare before/after cost and eval metrics. here's a screenshot (shared).

[36:40] Samir: any gotchas with cloud nat and large batch sizes? we've seen egress spikes.
[36:48] Lucas: yes, batching can increase ephemeral egress. if you're in a VPC peered private deployment, egress stays internal; for hosted you'll see egress to the cloud region. Optimize simulates egress impact as part of the suggestion.

[37:30] June Park: can we require mTLS between our services and your dedicated pool?
[37:38] Maya: yes, for Dedicated we support mTLS termination and mutual certs for stronger identity.

[38:15] (minor audio, people typing)

[39:00] Priya: final thought — for the PR gating evals, can we set both absolute thresholds and relative regressions?
[39:08] Neeta: yes, both supported. you can fail a PR on absolute score < 0.78 and/or relative drop > 3%.

[40:00] Lucas: i pasted the quickstart link in chat — github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart (placeholder) — contains the examples we walked through.
[40:28] Priya: thanks for that.

[41:15] Maya: any other blockers?
[41:22] Omar: none from infra, we need the smoke test results and security packet.

[41:35] Priya: will you include the helm hook snippet for secret sync? that will help platform team approve.
[41:42] Lucas: yep will include.

[42:00] (planning logistics, calendar invites)

[43:10] Maya: final administrative — who should I copy on the follow-up? Priya, Omar, June, Samir?
[43:20] Priya: yes, please include June and Samir.

[43:40] Maya: great — recap in chat in 10 minutes with links + next steps. thanks all.

[44:10] (some small goodbyes)
[44:25] Omar: appreciate it, talk soon.
[44:33] Priya: thanks everyone.
[44:40] (recording continues with short silence until auto-stop at 48:00)

End of transcript.
